Bayern Munich assistant coach Aaron Danks on Tuesday praised Harry Kane after his Ballon d’Or win, saying the striker will already be focused on scoring his “next goal.” Kane, 33, was awarded the prestigious honour in his hometown of London on Monday evening, breaking through to win the award for the first time. Englishman Danks, who is in the dugout while head coach Vincent Kompany recovers in hospital from a virus, said receiving the game’s highest individual award would not change the England captain’s mindset. “I am really happy for him and proud of what he’s achieved. I know Harry and his full focus will now be on his next goal, his next performances, his next games,” Danks said at a press conference on Tuesday. “He’ll be straight back into that professional, humble mindset that got him to this level.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources Kane had won several goalscoring honours and was runner-up in the Premier League and Champions League with Tottenham but did not break through for a first-team trophy until after he moved to Bayern in 2023. Since arriving in Munich, Kane has won two Bundesliga titles and the German Cup, along with making the Champions League semi-finals in two of three seasons at Bayern. Danks said the former Spurs striker was finally getting the recognition he deserves. “I remember years ago when he was back home in England, and everybody spoke about him not winning trophies, but if you looked at his career and what he was achieving, he was having a fantastic career. He’ll train, practice this afternoon and be available for tomorrow… Our full focus is on the game tomorrow,” Danks said. Danks also said he had visited Kompany in hospital and revealed the manager, who was rushed to hospital on Friday after collapsing on the training pitch, was improving. “He’s in good spirits. It looks like every day he’s getting better. There are no major updates in terms of diagnosis or a return to work; it’s very calm, let him rest, let him recover.” After seven games, Bayern sit top of the Bundesliga, level on points but ahead on goal difference from Borussia Dortmund, with the two sides facing off in Munich on Saturday.
